text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says Jordan is entering the period of peace, development and self-sufficiency. Says economic reforms aim to tackle the causes of poverty and unemployment.
- Srour wins re-election as speaker of house of deputies, winning 46 votes to Islamist candidate Kilani's 29.
- Landowners of Hussein refugee camp want compensation for their land since 1970, lawyers say.
- Dustour learns that Ministry of Water and Irrigation has issued orders for 16 million dinar ($22.6 million) infrastructure on east bank of Dead Sea.
- Jordan deserves to achieve more in the period of peace than it did during the period of war and conflict, King Hussein tells opening session of parliament.
- 3,000-strong electricians union says it carrying out "open" strikes this morning in all parts of Amman Electrical Company until the company responds to its pay demands.

- Deputy head of engineers' union calls for speedy implementation of understanding agreed with Ministry of Public Works last month. Union to call for doubling pension to 360 dinars a month from 180 dinars.
- King Hussein says the government continues to restructure all economic sectors.
- New status with U.S. will boost Jordan's armed forces, king says.
- Lovers sentenced to death for killing woman's husband with rat poison.
- Japan considering $76 million loan to boost Jordan's tourism industry, ambassador says.
